h.select_rule: Discard hypotheses conditioning on the edited field's own value or making the edit inert. Keep 10 spanning at least five mechanism families, with at most two resting on redundancy or substitution, preferring those with a two-sided argument and a sharp refuting comparison.
h.strategy: Experts find three patterns obvious: conditioning on the edited field's own value, conditions that make the edit inert, and 'capacity is already supplied elsewhere, so the edit adds less'. At most two hypotheses may rest on that last redundancy argument. Draw the rest from distinct mechanism families. Optimization and gradient flow: an edit changes trainability depending on another part. Signal scale or variance: summing or merging streams changes magnitudes. Effective depth versus width. Regularization or overfitting: added capacity hurts when another part already fits easily. Complementarity: two different component types help more together than either predicts alone. Each hypothesis must couple two different fields, and no condition setting may appear more than twice. Write each 'why' in two parts: the mechanism and the outcome it predicts, then the strongest argument for the opposite direction and why you reject it.

hyps.why: An input-to-output identity shortcut adds more when the other path into the output is a deep conv chain that benefits from a short gradient route.
Two stacked average pools on 0->2->3 low-pass the small images twice and erase detail, so the second pool hurts more.
Pooling learned conv features gives useful local invariance, whereas pooling raw-input copies only blurs.
With an identity shortcut already reaching the output, an extra deep conv on 1->2 adds mostly overfitting capacity and little validation gain.
A skip on 0->2 parallel to a conv series path 0->1->2 forms a residual block, which helps most when the branch is a deep nonlinear conv.
With edge 5 removed, edge 4 is the only route from node 1 and node 2 to the output, so its capacity is scarcer and upgrading it matters more.
Without edge 4, edge 0's features reach the output only via the longer 1->2->3 route, which limits its influence.
A 3x3 conv already feeding the output sum from the input makes another 3x3 conv from node 1 partly redundant, so gains saturate.
With a strong 3x3 conv already supplying the output, an additional conv on 2->3 adds diminishing capacity.
When node 1 already feeds the output through a 3x3 conv, a parallel 3x3 conv from the input is largely redundant.
